### 1.1-1.3 Problem Analysis

The issue describes a **caching problem** in the apischema library's deserialization mechanism:

**Key Technical Details:**
- **Methods involved**: `deserialize()`, `deserializer()`  
- **Classes**: `Foo`, `Conversion`, `catch_value_error`, `ValidationError`
- **Problem**: Internal caching prevents newly added deserializers from taking effect when deserialization has already occurred

**Clear Problem Statement:**
When `deserialize()` is called on a type before registering a new deserializer for that type, the caching mechanism incorrectly prevents the new deserializer from being recognized in subsequent calls.

### 1.4 Steps to Reproduce:
1. Define a custom class `Foo` inheriting from `int`
2. Call `deserialize(Foo, 1)` - this triggers internal caching
3. Register a new deserializer using `deserializer(Conversion(...))` for str→Foo conversion
4. Attempt to deserialize `Foo` from `'1'` - should raise `ValidationError` but doesn't due to caching

### 1.5 Best Practices for Testing/Fixing:
- Need to understand the caching invalidation mechanism
- Should ensure cache is properly invalidated when new deserializers are registered
- Must maintain backward compatibility
- Fix should be minimal and focused on the caching logic

     1	# apischema
     2	
     3	JSON (de)serialization, GraphQL and JSON schema generation using Python typing.
     4	
     5	*apischema* makes your life easier when dealing with API data.
     6	
     7	## Documentation
     8	
     9	[https://wyfo.github.io/apischema/](https://wyfo.github.io/apischema/)
    10	
    11	## Install
    12	```shell
    13	pip install apischema
    14	```
    15	It requires only Python 3.6+ (and dataclasses [official backport](https://pypi.org/project/dataclasses/) for version 3.6 only)
    16	
    17	*PyPy3* is fully supported.
    18	
    19	## Why another library?
    20	
    21	(If you wonder how this differs from the *pydantic* library, see the [dedicated section of the documentation(https://wyfo.github.io/apischema/0.17/difference_with_pydantic) — there are many differences.)
    22	
    23	This library fulfills the following goals:
    24	
    25	- stay as close as possible to the standard library (dataclasses, typing, etc.) — as a consequence we do not need plugins for editors/linters/etc.;
    26	- avoid object-oriented limitations — do not require a base class — thus handle easily every type (`Foo`, `list[Bar]`, `NewType(Id, int)`, etc.) the same way.
    27	- be adaptable, provide tools to support any types (ORM, etc.);
    28	- avoid dynamic things like using raw strings for attributes name - play nicely with your IDE.
    29	
    30	No known alternative achieves all of this, and apischema is also [(a lot) faster](https://wyfo.github.io/apischema/0.17/optimizations_and_benchmark#benchmark) than all of them.
    31	
    32	On top of that, because APIs are not only JSON, *apischema* is also a complete GraphQL library
    33	
    34	> Actually, *apischema* is even adaptable enough to enable support of competitor libraries in a few dozens of line of code ([pydantic support example](https://wyfo.github.io/apischema/0.17/examples/pydantic_support) using [conversions feature](https://wyfo.github.io/apischema/0.17/conversions))
    35	
    36	## Example
    37	
    38	```python
    39	from collections.abc import Collection
    40	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
    41	from uuid import UUID, uuid4
    42	
    43	import pytest
    44	from graphql import print_schema
    45	
    46	from apischema import ValidationError, deserialize, serialize
    47	from apischema.graphql import graphql_schema
    48	from apischema.json_schema import deserialization_schema
    49	
    50	
    51	# Define a schema with standard dataclasses
    52	@dataclass
    53	class Resource:
    54	    id: UUID
    55	    name: str
    56	    tags: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
    57	
    58	
    59	# Get some data
    60	uuid = uuid4()
    61	data = {"id": str(uuid), "name": "wyfo", "tags": ["some_tag"]}
    62	# Deserialize data
    63	resource = deserialize(Resource, data)
    64	assert resource == Resource(uuid, "wyfo", {"some_tag"})
    65	# Serialize objects
    66	assert serialize(Resource, resource) == data
    67	# Validate during deserialization
    68	with pytest.raises(ValidationError) as err:  # pytest checks exception is raised
    69	    deserialize(Resource, {"id": "42", "name": "wyfo"})
    70	assert err.value.errors == [
    71	    {"loc": ["id"], "err": "badly formed hexadecimal UUID string"}
    72	]
    73	# Generate JSON Schema
    74	assert deserialization_schema(Resource) == {
    75	    "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema#",
    76	    "type": "object",
    77	    "properties": {
    78	        "id": {"type": "string", "format": "uuid"},
    79	        "name": {"type": "string"},
    80	        "tags": {
    81	            "type": "array",
    82	            "items": {"type": "string"},
    83	            "uniqueItems": True,
    84	            "default": [],
    85	        },
    86	    },
    87	    "required": ["id", "name"],
    88	    "additionalProperties": False,
    89	}
    90	
    91	
    92	# Define GraphQL operations
    93	def resources(tags: Collection[str] | None = None) -> Collection[Resource] | None:
    94	    ...
    95	
    96	
    97	# Generate GraphQL schema
    98	schema = graphql_schema(query=[resources], id_types={UUID})
    99	schema_str = """\
   100	type Query {
   101	  resources(tags: [String!]): [Resource!]
   102	}
   103	
   104	type Resource {
   105	  id: ID!
   106	  name: String!
   107	  tags: [String!]!
   108	}"""
   109	assert print_schema(schema) == schema_str
   110	```
   111	*apischema* works out of the box with your data model.
   112
